finding.claim: The /rss endpoint passes the user-supplied `u` query parameter straight to URI.open, which fetches the URL. An attacker can make the server request internal hosts (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 metadata, private ranges) and read the first 400 bytes of the response. The response body is returned to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF. Depending on the Ruby version, open-uri's Kernel#open behavior may also allow more than HTTP.
finding.sink: URI.open(params[:u]).read, with the response returned in the HTTP body

trace.note: params[:u] is passed unvalidated to URI.open, and the body is read
the first 400 bytes of the fetched content are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, or IP allowlist or denylist. No redirect restrictions, so open-uri follows redirects. No DNS pinning. Nothing validates the value on this path.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes the unauthenticated params[:u] straight to URI.open(...).read and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes, with no validation (the TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:5 is only used in the separate /trusted route at app.rb:14).
